methodology.note: Dates labeled approximate or traditional are not presented as exact chronology. Formal definitions are distinguished from earliest surviving witnesses and reform events.

events.label: c. 1900–1700 BC
events.title: Patriarchal age: Abraham, Isaac, Jacob
events.summary: The ancestral narratives locate Israel’s beginnings in the patriarchs and the promises made to Abraham and his descendants.

events.label: c. 13th c. BC
events.title: Exodus and Sinai covenant
events.summary: Israel’s deliverance from Egypt and covenant at Sinai form a central biblical pattern for salvation, law, worship, and later Christian typology.

events.label: c. 13th–12th c. BC
events.title: Settlement / conquest traditions
events.summary: Joshua presents Israel taking possession of Canaan; Judges follows the pre-monarchic period.

events.label: c. 1000 BC
events.title: Davidic kingdom and covenant
events.summary: David’s kingship and dynasty become a major foundation for later messianic expectation.

events.label: c. 930 BC
events.title: Kingdom divided: Israel and Judah
events.summary: After Solomon the monarchy divides into northern Israel and southern Judah.

events.label: 722/721 BC
events.title: Fall of the Northern Kingdom
events.summary: Assyria destroys the Northern Kingdom of Israel.

events.label: 587 BC
events.title: Fall of Jerusalem and Babylonian exile
events.summary: Babylon destroys Jerusalem and Judah enters exile.

events.label: 538 BC onward
events.title: Persian period and return from exile
events.summary: Persian rule permits Judean restoration; Ezra-Nehemiah preserve major restoration traditions.

events.label: 515 BC
events.title: Second Temple completed
events.summary: The rebuilt Temple anchors the post-exilic and Second Temple period.

events.label: 175–164 BC
events.title: Antiochus IV and Maccabean crisis
events.summary: Seleucid persecution and resistance form the setting of 1–2 Maccabees.

events.label: 164 BC
events.title: Temple rededication
events.summary: The Maccabean restoration of Temple worship stands near the close of the Old Testament historical horizon.

events.label: c. 6–4 BC
events.title: Birth of Jesus Christ
events.summary: The Incarnation opens the climactic fulfillment of Israel’s messianic hope.

events.label: c. AD 27–30
events.title: Public ministry of Jesus
events.summary: Jesus proclaims the Kingdom, teaches, heals, gathers disciples, and prepares the New Covenant.

events.label: c. AD 30
events.title: Passion, Resurrection and Ascension
events.summary: The Paschal Mystery stands at the center of Christian faith and apostolic preaching.

events.label: c. AD 30
events.title: Pentecost and public apostolic mission
events.summary: The Holy Spirit empowers the apostolic witness and the Church’s mission.

events.label: c. AD 49
events.title: Council of Jerusalem
events.summary: Acts 15 records an apostolic council resolving a major question concerning Gentile Christians.

events.label: c. AD 64–67
events.title: Martyrdoms of Peter and Paul
events.summary: Ancient Christian tradition locates the martyrdoms of Peter and Paul at Rome under Nero.

events.label: AD 70
events.title: Destruction of Jerusalem and the Second Temple
events.summary: Roman forces destroy Jerusalem and the Temple, reshaping Jewish and Christian history.

events.label: c. AD 96
events.title: 1 Clement
events.summary: The Roman church’s letter known as 1 Clement is among the earliest surviving post-apostolic Christian writings.

events.label: c. AD 107
events.title: Ignatius of Antioch’s letters
events.summary: Ignatius writes to churches while being taken to martyrdom, witnessing to bishop-centered ecclesial life and Eucharistic faith.

events.label: early 2nd c.
events.title: Polycarp to the Philippians
events.summary: Polycarp preserves an early pastoral witness closely connected with the apostolic generation.

events.label: c. AD 155
events.title: Justin Martyr’s First Apology
events.summary: Justin describes Christian worship, Baptism, and Eucharistic practice in second-century Rome.

events.label: c. AD 180
events.title: Irenaeus, Against Heresies
events.summary: Irenaeus argues from apostolic tradition, succession, Scripture, and the rule of faith against Gnostic systems.

events.label: AD 325
events.title: First Council of Nicaea
events.summary: The council responds to Arianism and confesses the Son’s true divinity.

events.label: AD 381
events.title: First Council of Constantinople
events.summary: The Nicene faith is reaffirmed and the Church’s confession of the Holy Spirit is articulated against contemporary errors.

events.label: AD 431
events.title: Council of Ephesus
events.summary: The council defends the unity of Christ’s person and the title Theotokos, Mother of God.

events.label: AD 451
events.title: Council of Chalcedon
events.summary: Chalcedon confesses the one person of Christ in two natures, divine and human.

events.label: after AD 451
events.title: Post-Chalcedonian separations
events.summary: Disputes surrounding Chalcedon contribute to enduring divisions among ancient Eastern Christian communities.

events.label: AD 787
events.title: Second Council of Nicaea
events.summary: The seventh ecumenical council addresses the iconoclast controversy and sacred images.

events.label: AD 1054 (long process)
events.title: East–West rupture conventionally dated to 1054
events.summary: The dissolution of communion between Eastern patriarchates and Rome developed through a long historical process, conventionally associated with 1054.

events.label: 11th c.
events.title: Gregorian Reform
events.summary: A broad medieval reform movement addressed clerical discipline, ecclesial governance, and freedom of the Church.

events.label: early 13th c.
events.title: Mendicant renewal
events.summary: Franciscan and Dominican movements become major forces of evangelical, pastoral, intellectual, and missionary renewal.

events.title: Western Schism
events.summary: Competing papal claimants divide Western Christendom until the crisis is resolved at Constance.

events.title: Council of Constance and end of Western Schism
events.summary: The council resolves the Western Schism; later conciliarist claims require careful distinction from Catholic teaching on primacy.

events.label: from 1517
events.title: Protestant Reformation
events.summary: Western reform controversies lead to multiple ecclesial communities separating from the Roman See.

events.title: Council of Trent and Catholic Reform
events.summary: Trent clarifies disputed doctrine and advances major Catholic disciplinary and pastoral reforms in response to the Reformation crisis.

events.title: First Vatican Council
events.summary: Vatican I treats revelation, faith and reason, and papal primacy and infallibility before being interrupted in 1870.

events.title: Second Vatican Council
events.summary: Vatican II addresses the Church, revelation, liturgy, ecumenism, mission, religious freedom, and the Church in the modern world.

events.title: 1983 Code of Canon Law
events.summary: The revised Latin Code implements legal renewal shaped by Vatican II.
events.source: Vatican Code of Canon Law introduction

events.label: late 1st / early 2nd c.
events.title: Didache
events.summary: Early church-order text addressing Christian morals, Baptism, fasting, Eucharistic prayer, and community order.

events.label: c. AD 107
events.title: Ignatius, Smyrnaeans
events.summary: Primary-source witness useful for studying Eucharist, ecclesial unity, and the bishop.

events.label: c. AD 155
events.title: Justin, First Apology 65–67
events.summary: Primary-source section commonly studied for Baptism, Eucharist, and Sunday Christian worship.

events.label: c. AD 180
events.title: Irenaeus, Against Heresies III
events.summary: Primary-source material important for apostolic tradition, succession, Scripture, and public catholic teaching.
